subject: maths
title: Comparing Angles: Acute, Right, Obtuse, Straight, Reflex and Revolution
seo_title: Year 4 Angles Worksheets: Acute, Obtuse, Reflex and Straight Angles (Free, Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Estimate and compare angles using angle names including acute, obtuse, straight angle, reflex and revolution, and recognise their relationship to a right angle
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on comparing angles: name acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex angles and a revolution, compare angles with a right angle, find angles in clocks, doors and shapes, and link turns to right angles. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4M04).
key_big: Compare every angle with a right angle: less is acute, more is obtuse, 2 right angles is straight.
key_sub: More than a straight angle is reflex, and a full turn (4 right angles) is a revolution. The size of an angle is the turn between its arms, not the length of the arms.
body_html:
Compare every angle with a right angle

An angle is the amount of turn between two arms. A right angle is a square corner: a quarter turn. Use it to name every other angle. The arc shows which angle is meant.

NameCompared with a right angle
Acute angleless than 1 right angle
Right angleexactly 1 right angle (a quarter turn)
Obtuse anglebetween 1 and 2 right angles
Straight angleexactly 2 right angles (a half turn)
Reflex anglebetween 2 and 4 right angles
Revolutionexactly 4 right angles (a full turn)

Turns make angles

Example

Mia faces north. She turns clockwise until she faces west. What angle has she turned through?

North to east, east to south, south to west: 3 right angles. That is more than a straight angle.

Answer: a reflex angle

Example

At 4 o’clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?

A right angle is 3 hour marks (3 o’clock) and a straight angle is 6 (6 o’clock). 4 is between them.

Answer: an obtuse angle

Compare two angles

Look at how far each angle turns. Is it less than, equal to or more than a right angle? A straight angle? The length of the arms does not matter.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking longer arms make a bigger angleLook at the turn between the arms, not the arm length
Calling a reflex angle obtuseCheck the arc. If it goes round the outside, past a straight line, it is reflex
Saying a straight line is “no angle”A half turn is an angle: a straight angle, 2 right angles
Thinking a tilted right angle is not a right angleTurning an angle does not change its size or name

faq.q: What are the angle names in Year 4 maths in Australia?
faq.a: Acute (less than a right angle), right, obtuse (between a right angle and a straight angle), straight (2 right angles), reflex (between a straight angle and a revolution) and revolution (a full turn).

faq.q: Do Year 4 students measure angles in degrees?
faq.a: No. In Year 4 students estimate and compare angles with a right angle. Measuring in degrees with a protractor starts in Year 5.
A reflex angle is greater than a straight angle (a half turn) but less than a revolution (a full turn). It is the angle on the outside of the arms.

faq.q: Why is a longer-armed angle not a bigger angle?
faq.a: The size of an angle is the amount of turn between its arms. Making the arms longer or shorter does not change the turn.

sets.title: Name the angle: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex, revolution

items.e: A straight angle is 2 right angles: a half turn. The two arms make a straight line.
A revolution is one whole turn: 4 right angles. The arm goes all the way round and ends where it started.
A reflex angle is greater than a straight angle but less than a revolution. The arc goes round the outside. The gap between the arms is small, but the marked angle is the big one.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: A right angle is a square corner: a quarter turn. The small square shows it. Turning the angle does not change its name.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle: narrower than a square corner.
A straight angle is 2 right angles: a half turn. The two arms make a straight line. Turning the angle does not change its name.
A reflex angle is greater than a straight angle but less than a revolution. The arc goes round the outside. The gap between the arms is small, but the marked angle is the big one.

items.q: How many right angles make a straight angle?
items.e: A straight angle is a half turn. A half turn is 2 quarter turns, so it is 2 right angles.
An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle.

No, it is a reflex angle

items.e: The arm has turned a half turn from the other arm. That turn is an angle: a straight angle (2 right angles).

items.q: An angle is greater than a straight angle but less than a revolution. What is it called?
items.e: Between a straight angle (a half turn) and a revolution (a full turn) is a reflex angle. An obtuse angle is less than a straight angle.
An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle.

items.q: An angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle. What is it called?
items.e: Between a right angle and a straight angle is an obtuse angle.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
c: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex, revolution
acute, right, obtuse, reflex, straight, revolution
right, acute, obtuse, straight, revolution, reflex
acute, obtuse, right, straight, reflex, revolution
items.e: Acute is less than a right angle. Obtuse is between a right angle and a straight angle. Reflex is between a straight angle and a revolution, which is the largest.
An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle.

c: Yes, it is an obtuse angle
No, it is a reflex angle
No, it is an acute angle
No, it is a straight angle
items.e: The arc goes round the outside. The gap between the arms looks obtuse, but the marked angle is greater than a straight angle, so it is reflex.

items.q: An angle is less than a right angle. What is it called?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle. An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle: narrower than a square corner.

items.q: How many right angles make a revolution?
items.e: A revolution is a full turn. A full turn is 4 quarter turns, so it is 4 right angles.

items.q: Which angle is one whole turn?
items.e: A revolution is one whole turn: the arm turns all the way round. A straight angle is only half a turn.

sets.title: Compare angles (arm length does not matter)

items.q: Angle P is a right angle. Angle Q is a little less than a right angle. Which angle is larger?
items.e: Angle Q is less than a right angle, so the right angle P is larger.
Angle Q is reflex: its arc goes round the outside, past a straight angle. Angle P is obtuse, less than a straight angle.
Y is acute, X is obtuse and Z is reflex. Look at the turn and the arc, not the arm length.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both are right angles (the small squares show it). Tilting an angle or making its arms longer does not change it.
A is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle. In B the gap looks obtuse, but the arc marks the reflex angle round the outside.
Angle P is reflex, so it is greater than a straight angle. Angle Q is obtuse, less than a straight angle.

items.q: Which angle is the largest?
items.e: B is obtuse, so it is greater than a right angle. A and D are acute and C is a right angle. B has the shortest arms, but arm length does not matter.

items.q: Which is always larger: an obtuse angle or an acute angle?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle. An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle. So the obtuse angle is always larger.
Angle P is obtuse and angle Q is acute. Long arms do not make an angle larger.

items.q: Aarav draws two angles. Angle P has arms 10 cm long and angle Q has arms 3 cm long. He says P must be the larger angle. Is he right?
c: Yes, longer arms make a larger angle
No, arm length does not change the size of an angle
items.e: The size of an angle is the amount of turn between the arms. You cannot tell which is larger from the arm lengths.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both angles open the same amount. Only the arms are different lengths, and arm length does not change an angle.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both are acute, but angle Q opens wider. Put one on top of the other to check.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Angle Q is obtuse and angle P is acute. Q is larger, even though its arms are shorter.

items.q: An angle is larger than 2 right angles but smaller than 4 right angles. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: 2 right angles make a straight angle and 4 make a revolution. Between them is a reflex angle.
Only the arc in D goes round more than a straight angle. A is obtuse: close to a straight angle, but less.
C is acute: less than a right angle. A is obtuse, B is a right angle and D is reflex.
Angle P is a straight angle. Angle Q is obtuse: it is less than a straight angle, even with longer arms.

items.q: Which is always larger: a straight angle or a reflex angle?
items.e: A reflex angle is greater than a straight angle, by definition.

items.q: Two angles are both obtuse. What do you know for sure?
c: Both are larger than a straight angle
Both are larger than a right angle
items.e: Every obtuse angle is greater than a right angle and less than a straight angle. Two obtuse angles can still be different sizes.

items.q: Which of these angles is smaller than a right angle?
items.e: Only an acute angle is less than a right angle. Obtuse, straight and reflex angles are all larger.

sets.title: Angles in shapes and everyday objects

items.q: What kind of angle is marked between the clock hands?
items.e: The hands are 2 hour marks apart. A right angle is 3 hour marks (3 o’clock), so this is less: acute.

items.q: The red arc goes clockwise from the minute hand to the hour hand. What kind of angle does it mark?
items.e: From 12 to 8 is 8 hour marks, more than 6 (a straight angle). So the marked angle is reflex. The gap on the other side is obtuse, but that is not the marked angle.

items.q: This door is seen from above. It opened from the dashed line. What kind of angle has it opened?
items.e: The door has opened past a square corner but not to a straight line, so the angle is obtuse.

c: No, it is an acute angle
No, it is a straight angle
Yes, it is an obtuse angle
No, it is a reflex angle
items.e: The corner points into the shape, so the angle inside is greater than a straight angle: reflex. The gap outside the shape is the obtuse one.

items.q: Which angle in this triangle is obtuse?
items.e: Angle C at the top opens wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. A and B are acute.
The screen leans back past a square corner, but not flat. That is an obtuse angle.

items.q: A right-angled triangle has 1 right angle. What kind of angles are the other 2?
items.e: The other 2 angles of a right-angled triangle together make 1 right angle, so each one is less than a right angle: acute.

items.q: This door is seen from above. It opened from the dashed line. What kind of angle has it opened?
items.e: The door has opened less than a square corner, so the angle is acute.

items.q: Grace opens a book and lays it flat on the table. What angle do the two covers make?
items.e: When the book lies flat, the covers make a straight line: a straight angle.

items.q: Which scissors are open wider?
c: They are open the same amount
items.e: The angle between the blades of Q is larger. P has longer blades, but long blades do not make a larger angle.

items.q: What kind of angle do the blades of these scissors make?
items.e: The blades open less than a square corner, so the angle is acute.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. What kind of angle is at the tip of one slice?
items.e: 2 slices make a quarter of the pizza: a right angle. One slice is half of that, so it is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked between the clock hands?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands make a square corner: a right angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked between the clock hands?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the hands point in opposite directions. They make a straight angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is at each corner of a give way sign (a triangle with equal sides)?
items.e: Each corner of an equilateral triangle is narrower than a square corner, so it is acute.
7 of the 8 slices are left. That is more than half the pizza (a straight angle) but less than a whole (a revolution), so the angle is reflex.
The marked corner points inwards. Inside the shape it is 3 right angles, more than a straight angle: reflex.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 2 equal halves. What kind of angle is at the centre of one half?
items.e: Half a pizza has a straight cut edge through the centre. Half a turn is a straight angle.
Each corner of a regular hexagon is wider than a square corner but less than a straight line: obtuse.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked between the clock hands?
items.e: The hands are 4 hour marks apart. That is more than 3 (a right angle) and less than 6 (a straight angle): obtuse.

items.q: An arm turns more than a quarter turn but less than a half turn. What kind of angle does it make?
items.e: More than a right angle but less than a straight angle is obtuse.

items.q: Liam faces west. He turns clockwise through 1 right angle. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Clockwise goes north, east, south, west, then back to north. 1 right angle clockwise from west is north.

items.q: An arm turns less than a quarter turn. What kind of angle does it make?
items.e: A quarter turn is a right angle. Less than that is an acute angle.

items.q: Two quarter turns make which angle?
items.e: 2 quarter turns make a half turn. A half turn is a straight angle.

items.q: Which of these is a reflex angle?
items.e: 1 right angle is a right angle, 2 make a straight angle and 4 make a revolution. 3 right angles is between a straight angle and a revolution: reflex.

items.q: Which turn makes a right angle?
items.e: A right angle is a quarter turn: a square corner.
A three-quarter turn is 3 right angles. That is more than a straight angle, so it is reflex.

items.q: The arm turns from the dashed line in the direction of the arrow. What angle does the turn make?
items.e: A quarter turn makes a right angle: a square corner.

items.q: Cooper faces north. He turns anticlockwise through 3 right angles. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Anticlockwise from north: west (1), south (2), east (3). So he faces east.

items.q: An arm turns more than a half turn but less than a full turn. What kind of angle does it make?
items.e: More than a straight angle but less than a revolution is reflex.

items.q: Kai faces south. He turns through a straight angle. Which way does he face now?
items.e: A straight angle is a half turn, so he faces the opposite way. North is opposite south.

The arm turns all the way round, back to the dashed line. A full turn is a revolution.

items.q: Which turn makes a revolution?
items.e: A revolution is one whole turn: a full turn, or 4 right angles.

items.q: How many right angles make a three-quarter turn?
items.e: Each right angle is a quarter turn. 3 quarter turns make a three-quarter turn.

items.q: Which turn makes a straight angle?
items.e: A straight angle is 2 right angles, and 2 quarter turns make a half turn.

items.q: The arm turns from the dashed line in the direction of the arrow. What angle does the turn make?
items.e: A half turn makes the arm point the opposite way. That is a straight angle: 2 right angles.

items.q: Ruby faces north. She turns clockwise until she faces south. What angle has she turned through?
items.e: North to south is a half turn: 2 right angles. That is a straight angle.

items.q: Amelia faces east. She turns clockwise until she faces north. What angle has she turned through?
items.e: Clockwise from east: south (1), west (2), north (3). 3 right angles is a reflex angle.

items.q: Charlotte turns from facing north to facing south. She says that makes no angle, because she is still on the same straight line. Is she right?
c: No, it is a right angle
No, it is a straight angle
items.e: Charlotte turned a half turn. A half turn is an angle: a straight angle, 2 right angles.

items.q: Matilda opens her laptop until the screen stands straight up from the keyboard. What angle do the screen and keyboard make?
items.e: Straight up from a flat keyboard is a square corner: a right angle.

items.q: Noah faces north. He makes a quarter turn clockwise, then a half turn clockwise. What angle has he turned through altogether?
items.e: 1 quarter turn + 2 quarter turns = 3 quarter turns: 3 right angles. That is a reflex angle.

items.q: At the beach, Ethan leans the back of his deckchair back. It is wider than a square corner but not flat. What angle do the seat and back make?
items.e: Wider than a right angle but less than a straight angle is obtuse.

items.q: The minute hand turns from 12 to 6. What angle has it turned through?
items.e: From 12 to 6 is halfway round the clock: a half turn. That is a straight angle.

items.q: Recess starts at 11:00 am and ends at 11:20 am. The minute hand turns from 12 to 4. What angle has it turned through?
items.e: 12 to 3 is a right angle. 12 to 4 is a bit more, but less than 12 to 6 (a straight angle). So it is obtuse.

items.q: A class plays a 10-minute game. The minute hand turns from 12 to 2. What angle has it turned through?
items.e: 12 to 2 is less than 12 to 3 (a right angle), so the angle is acute.

items.q: A spelling test starts at 9:00 am and ends at 9:45 am. The minute hand turns from 12 to 9. What angle has it turned through?
items.e: 12 to 3, 3 to 6 and 6 to 9 is 3 right angles: a three-quarter turn. That is a reflex angle.

items.q: At the skate park, Zara spins her skateboard all the way round once, a “360”. What angle has the board turned through?
items.e: All the way round once is a full turn: a revolution.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices and Lachlan eats 1. What kind of angle do the 3 slices left make at the centre?
items.e: 3 quarter slices make 3 right angles. That is more than a straight angle: reflex.

items.q: On a school excursion, Ava walks north, then turns right to walk east. What angle did she turn through?
items.e: North to east is a quarter turn clockwise: a right angle.

items.q: At which time do the hands of an analog clock make an acute angle?
items.e: At 2 o’clock the hands are 2 hour marks apart, less than a right angle (3). 5 o’clock is obtuse.

items.q: Sienna opens her scissors a little to cut a ribbon. What kind of angle do the blades make?
items.e: A little open is less than a square corner, so the blades make an acute angle.

items.q: Mei’s family cuts a pizza into 4 equal slices. What kind of angle is at the tip of each slice?
items.e: 4 equal slices are 4 quarter turns round the centre. A quarter turn is a right angle.

items.q: At 9 o’clock, what angle do the hands of an analog clock make?
items.e: The minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand to 9. That is 3 hour marks apart: a square corner, a right angle.

items.q: At which time do the hands of an analog clock make an obtuse angle?
items.e: At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 hour marks apart: more than a right angle (3) and less than a straight angle (6). 3 o’clock is a right angle, 1 o’clock is acute and 6 o’clock is straight.

items.q: Jack turns the garden tap on with a half turn. What angle does the handle turn through?
items.e: A half turn is a straight angle: 2 right angles.

items.q: Oliver and William each cut a round pizza into 8 equal slices. William’s pizza is much bigger, so his slices have longer sides. William says the tip of his slice is a bigger angle. Is he right?
c: No, the tips are the same size
Yes, longer sides make a bigger angle
No, the smaller pizza’s slice has a bigger angle
items.e: Both pizzas are cut into 8 equal slices, so each tip turns the same amount: half a right angle. Longer sides do not change the angle.

items.q: Leo opens the classroom door just a little, less than a square corner, to peek out. What angle has the door opened?
items.e: Less than a square corner (a right angle) is an acute angle.

items.q: Isla faces the beach to the east. She turns anticlockwise until she faces south. What angle has she turned through?
items.e: Anticlockwise from east: north, west, south. That is 3 right angles, a reflex angle. (Turning clockwise would only be 1 right angle.)

items.q: The minute hand turns for exactly one hour. What angle has it turned through?
items.e: In one hour the minute hand goes all the way round once: a full turn, a revolution.
